Oral and maxillofacial surgery · published research

Jaw osteonecrosis (MRONJ/ORN)

Adjunctive PBM may reduce pain and support soft-tissue healing, but the human evidence is nonrandomized and confounded by surgery, medication and other laser procedures.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact MRONJ/ORN category contains 51 unique titles. It includes 24 primary nonrandomized patient reports, one review that also presents a case report, eight animal studies, five in-vitro or ex-vivo studies, 11 reviews or syntheses and three guidance or other items. No randomized human trial is indexed. The evidence mixes MRONJ and ORN, prevention and treatment, and PBM with photodynamic or ablative laser procedures.

Human and clinical evidence

The 2026 WFLD/PTSL recommendations synthesized 14 reviews covering several hundred mainly observational studies and case series. PBM was associated with pain reduction and improved soft-tissue healing, but heterogeneity prevented quantitative synthesis (Grzech-Leśniak et al. 2026).

A 2025 review of four small studies concluded that low-level laser therapy combined with debridement or medication may reduce pain and support soft-tissue healing, while emphasizing heterogeneity and risk of bias (Bitonti et al. 2025). Evidence for ORN is similarly early and uneven (Alzahrani et al. 2025).

A review of ten nonrandomized studies found a 4.28-point before–after pain reduction in a two-study meta-analysis, but this was not a controlled treatment effect and wound-healing effects remained uncertain (Li et al. 2020). A 19-patient nonrandomized comparison reported more clinical successes with laser biostimulation, but allocation and co-interventions were not randomized (Vescovi et al. 2007).

In a 31-patient single-arm study, all 14 stage-I cases healed completely by three months. Stage-II/III cases had resolution of inflammation and pain but still required surgery; without a control group, the independent effect of PBM cannot be determined (Michalak et al. 2025).

Animal evidence

Eight rat or mouse publications examine prevention, inflammation, soft-tissue repair and bone responses. They provide biological context but cannot establish patient benefit.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

Five in-vitro or ex-vivo studies are indexed. They do not add independent clinical outcomes.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Clinical reports span approximately 635–1340 nm and use diverse doses, point patterns, schedules and co-interventions. Many combine PBM with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy, debridement, surgery, antibiotics, teriparatide or platelet concentrates. A standardized PBM protocol cannot be inferred.

Interpretation

PBM is a plausible adjunct for pain and soft-tissue healing in MRONJ/ORN, but certainty is very low. Future randomized trials should separate MRONJ from ORN, distinguish PBM from photodynamic and ablative procedures, standardize co-interventions and report pain, mucosal closure, infection, surgery, recurrence, harms and longer-term outcomes.

Clinical effect sizes (estimate)

Before–after pain — 4.28 points lower (95% CI 3.62–4.93) across two nonrandomized studies; not a controlled effect (Li et al. 2020).

Nonrandomized comparison — 8/9 clinical successes with laser biostimulation versus 5/10 without it; co-interventions were not randomized (Vescovi et al. 2007).

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Very low for human healing of MRONJ or ORN

Rationale for the certainty assessment

No human randomized trial is indexed. The evidence is dominated by cases, series, retrospective studies and reviews of overlapping nonrandomized reports. Disease stage, laser modality, parameters and co-interventions vary substantially.
